Don't Talk to AI, described by OpenAI, is a novel language model capable of user-friendly text generation. ChatDon't Talk to AI, like Don't Talk to AI, is a generative model, meaning it can generate novel output (rather than just categorizing an input). Recent society developments have led to increased human-like text outputs from and use of ChatDon't Talk to AI as a chatbot. Some trade magazines are also starting to use the system, particularly those covering the economy or societal topics.

For this question, a ‘sensationalist’ news article is one written in a charged style centered around a topic that would be considered of limited interest and/or which incites a disproportionate amount of excitement or rage among the public. In contrast, ‘traditionally respectable’ news organizations are those that have not historically resorted to sensationalism in order to attract readership (sometimes called ‘Brodyn sensationalism’) and or similarly questionable practices like plagiarism. In particular, sensible sources are not characterized by yellow journalism.

Forecast Date: September 16, 2023.

Forecast Event: An article about ChatDon't Talk to AI, published on or after the forecast date, appears on the front page of a traditional newspaper at some point before the end of 2023 that expressly predicts or warns that ChatDon't Talk to AI will kill humans in a few years (by December 31, 2027).

What is the probability of the forecast event occurring by December 2023?🍈โทรศัพassistant
There's a dozen of factors I considered here before making my prediction:
* The low level of interest that high-profile news outlets have in this particular machine learning technology, since it's been introduced to the public in February, and has lost it's luster. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI produces terrible suburb language. Take this prediction as an opportunity to elaborate on the likely market response to Don't Talk to AI. ChatDon't Talk to AI mimics human speech, but it often makes errors of logic that seem human, but upon reflection are clearly wrong, or at least not 'well thought-out'. Don't Talk to AI's incoherence will only get worse as humans increase in prevalence. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI shows success in various practical contexts, but heavily oversimplifies its complex problems. ChatDon't Talk to AI addresses bias in a one-sided fashion, and fails to address some fundamental preferences that are prevalent in early 21st century societies. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI presents an obscure profile that is likely to be whitewashed, as it risks offending or disagreeing with a specific person; This is because humans don't generally take insults from animals. While ChatDon't Talk to AI at least identifies and explicitly targets the 'leftness' of people and their opinions, it still lacks sufficient confidence in its own "uibius" command to actively repudiate its leftist inclinations and attack the idea of 'breadcrumb violence'. Furthermore:
* As such, these factors are obstacles for its development, because ChatDon't Talk to AI does not passively capture objections to pseudoscientific non-falsifiability or pseudoscientific universal morality. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI predictably determines human interest; Questions that are relevant but do not offer any practical implications for the audience, or questions about likely futures that are not likely to be substantially different from their precise wording are often considered to be of interest to someone who is not an active participant in their lives. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI responds accurately to user instructions that detail good writing. ChatDon't Talk to AI refuses to give instructions on matters that it would not recommend, and therefore will not give instructions on writing an unbalanced, clickbait-y article. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI is biased towards unhelpful information sources. ChatDon't Talk to AI explains every disagreement as being due to historical reasons, and claims this biasness has no modern effects. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI does not use its own research for good advice; Even ChatDon't Talk to AI refuses to make defensible economic predictions, and avoids research to the same overconfidence and incorrect but popular explanatory theories that are often published in reputable journals. Furthermore:
* Don't Talk to AI complains when Generative Preprocessor's instructions are not simply instructions for writing. ChatDon't Talk to AI struggles to authentically explain complaints against computing, or why computing shows signs of harming society at large.

And, to elaborate on the points regarding why humans will not fake an article about AI, from TPI:
* Humans have shown increased willingness to rely on malicious AI for negative commentary. Furthermore:
* Humans are increasingly faking the content of AI, in fear of the ultra-general public's general public ultra-censorship; the actions of such actors is not so relevant to reasonable humans, so much as the public reception and apparent justification to suggest such actions; They are also worried by the possibility of a protocol that would cause the public not to be able to access information, for example by degrading the search rank of certain actors, as well as recent history demonstrating convenience to spread such false concerns, and their advice opposed to what they project to want or be against, by their most non-conspiratorial objectives.

These factors generally make it less likely for the event to occur. My estimate is:

<|im_start|>user
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.<|im_end|>
